(April 29–June 13) |prevseason=[[2011 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A|2011]] |nextseason=[[2013 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A|2013]] }} The '''2012 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol de la Serie A''' (known as the '''2012 Copa Credife Serie A''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 54th season of the [[Ecuadorian Serie A|Serie A]], [[Ecuador]]'s premier [[Association football|football]] league. The season began on February 3 and ended in December 2012. [[Sociedad Deportivo Quito|Deportivo Quito]] was the defending champion. They were succeeded by [[Barcelona Sporting Club|Barcelona]], who won their record-breaking 14th title. ==Format== On the night of December 6, 2011, the [[Ecuadorian Football Federation]] determined that the format for 2012 will the same as the previous season.{{cite web |url=http://www.ecuafutbol.org/UI/detalle.aspx?seccion=1&categserie=7&nivel=0&subnivel=0&id=21038&tabla=N |title=Campeonato Nacional 2012 se Jugará con Mismo Sistema Desde 5 de Febrero |trans-title=2012 Campeonato Nacional will be played with the same format starting on February 5 |language=es |publisher=[[Ecuadorian Football Federation]] |access-date=December 7, 2011 |date=December 6, 2011 |archive-date=April 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200404231424/http://www.ecuafutbol.org/UI/detalle.aspx?seccion=1&categserie=7&nivel=0&subnivel=0&id=21038&tabla=N |url-status=dead }} ==Teams== Twelve teams competed in the 2012 Serie A season, ten of whom remained from the previous season. [[Club Deportivo ESPOLI|ESPOLI]] and [[Imbabura Sporting Club|Imbabura]] were relegated last season after accumulating the fewest points in the [[2011 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A#Aggregate table|2011 season aggregate table]]. They will be replaced by [[Club Deportivo Técnico Universitario|Técnico Universitario]]{{cite web |url=http://www.elcomercio.com/deportes/futbol/Tecnico-Universitario-festejo-Azogues-Serie_0_579542165.html |title=Técnico Universitario festejó en Azogues su retorno a la Serie A |trans-title=Técnico Universitario celebrated in Azogues their return to the Primera A |language=es |publisher=[[El Comercio (Ecuador)|El Comercio]] |date=October 26, 2011 |access-date=December 8, 2011 }} and [[Club Social y Deportivo Macará|Macará]],{{cite web |url=http://www.elcomercio.com/deportes/futbol/Ambato-fiesta-ascenso-Macara_0_594540547.html |title=Ambato está de fiesta por el retorno del Macará a la Primera A |trans-title=Ambato is celebrating the return of Macará to the Primera A |language=es |publisher=[[El Comercio (Ecuador)|El Comercio]] |date=November 25, 2011 |access-date=December 8, 2011 }} the 2011 [[Ecuadorian Serie B|Serie B]] winner and runner-up, respectively. Both teams from [[Ambato, Ecuador|Ambato]] are making returns to the Serie A.
